note: Recommendation levels, asserted by both languages from this one file.
server/tests/test_model_recommendation.py checks the shipped catalog carries these values;
Two tables that agree today would drift; one table cannot.
The stage keys narrow recommendation_llm rather than replacing it. A model measured end to
end -- every NVIDIA and Ollama Cloud entry -- has one number and both stages read it, so
adding these keys migrated nothing. Local Ollama models were measured per stage and the two
stages disagree, which is why the keys exist at all.
'absent' means not measured for that stage. It is not a zero: the picker shows an em dash,
and 1 is reserved for 'measured and poor'.

stage1.material: Japanese n/6 and English n/6 attempts that came back as usable normalized DDL, plus explicit-rule violations
stage1.5: 6/6 in both languages and zero explicit-rule violations
stage1.4: 6/6 in both languages, violations unrecorded or slight
stage1.3: 6/6 in one language, the other breaks down

stage2.material: coverage over 28 sentences of the five complex cases, plus the three failure kinds (budget / malformed / transport)
stage2.5: coverage 70% or more and no failures of any kind

excluded: Capacity (GB) is not an axis. It is in the label and the comment (adjudicated 2026-07-30).
Speed is not an axis (adjudicated 2026-07-27, narrowed 2026-07-29 to developer mode only).

note: The hover card splits the recommendation into two rows for a model measured per stage,
so reading one stage does not mean switching tabs to find the other. A model measured
end to end keeps one row: two rows would print the same stars twice and imply a
measurement nobody took. Vision is never split -- the stage keys narrow the LLM level
and say nothing about reading an image.
split: null means one row. Otherwise the two strings the card prints.
